title: AC1021 TABLE per-row border CMC lossless DXF audit
decision: Keep all 18 per-row border CMC slots and border color override mask output-refused for the general TABLE profile.
scope: Determine whether arbitrary title/header/data border colors can be represented losslessly by TABLE entity DXF fields.

oda.document: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
findings: The 18-bit border-color mask selects 18 independent CMC values across title, header and data rows.
Each row carries six ordered categories: horizontal top, horizontal inside, horizontal bottom, vertical left, vertical inside and vertical right.
Those six categories use DXF group-code families 64, 65, 66, 63, 68 and 69 respectively in the DWG specification's encoding table.

autodesk.title: TABLE (DXF)
findings: TABLE groups 63 and 64 are entity-level border/background color values and may have one entry for each cell type.
TABLE groups 65, 66, 68 and 69 are entity-level horizontal-inside, horizontal-bottom, vertical-inside and vertical-right border colors with no per-cell-type repeat declaration.
The same groups are separately documented for individual cell overrides, which does not create row-specific entity-level slots.

reasoning: Groups 63/64 can carry the title/header/data values for the vertical-left and horizontal-top categories, subject to color-method conversion evidence.

The remaining four categories have one entity-level DXF value each but up to three independent DWG row values each. For example, distinct selected title and data horizontal-inside CMC values cannot both be represented by one group-65 entity-level value.

CMC may also contain methods, RGB, color names/books and flags beyond a plain indexed color. These cannot be flattened into one shared DXF value without a narrower proven profile and explicit preservation policy.
implementation: No code change. Existing strict writer refusal for nonzero border-color override masks or retained CMC state is the correct general-profile behavior.
qualification_limits: This resolves the general lossless-mapping question by a representational counterexample; it does not claim that no narrower equality-constrained projection could ever be implemented.
No physical producer sample or native render check was used or needed to establish that the singular DXF groups cannot carry arbitrary distinct row values.
No support claim is promoted. Per-row border colors remain output-refused.
